artworks.title: Black-throated Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two Black-throated Buntings perched on flowering plants. The artwork depicts two colorful birds standing on branches of a plant, with one bird above the other. The plant has long, slender green leaves and a stem with clusters of bright yellow flowers. The birds are detailed, showcasing their vibrant colors, with chestnut and brown hues across their backs and wings, and yellow accents around their throats and heads. The painting captures the birds among the foliage in a style reminiscent of John James Audubon's detailed bird studies.

artworks.title: Bank Swallow and Violet-green Swallow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of swallows flying and nesting near cliffs. The image displays a combination of vibrant violet-green and bank swallows in action above a cliffside, showcasing their colorful plumage against a pale sky. Numerous swallows are depicted in flight or near a nest set in the rock face of the cliff. The artwork emphasizes the grace and motion of the birds, highlighting their streamlined bodies and delicate wings as they inhabit the natural rocky environment. This painting is done in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: White Heron
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a white heron. The bird is depicted with its long neck arched downward and its eyes focused. Its feathers are detailed in shades of white and grey. The heron's beak is yellow. The background shows lush green reeds and grass, mounds, rocks, and a small creature resembling a crab on the ground. The sky is a soft blue.

artworks.title: Glossy Ibis
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Glossy Ibis in a natural setting. The artwork features a Glossy Ibis with colorful plumage standing on a slope near water. The background includes a rural landscape with wooden structures, trees, tall grasses, and flowering plants.

artworks.title: Nuttall's Starling, Yellow-headed Troopial and Bullock's Oriole
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Four birds are perched on a branch. The uppermost bird is black with a red patch on its wing. Below it, a bird with brown and tan feathers leans downward. Another bird has a yellow head and black body with white accents. The last bird has an orange body, black wings, and white markings. The color palette includes black, red, brown, tan, yellow, and orange, with the branch in muted brown tones. The birds are arranged vertically on the branch.

artworks.title: Red-cockaded Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds perched on a tree trunk. The composition features a central brown tree trunk with detailed bark texture, upon which three woodpeckers are depicted. Below, two birds are climbing opposite sides of the trunk. Both have black and white striped patterns with red patches near their eyes. At the top, a third bird is resting on a branch with its head pulled in. The painting has a background of soft cream color, highlighting the birds and tree. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Lark Finch, Prairie Finch and Brown Song Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows four birds perched and positioned among sparse vegetation. The largest bird is brown and gray with white and reddish accents on its head, perched on a branch in the upper portion of the image. Below and slightly to the right, there is a black bird with a distinctive blue beak perched on the same branch. Lower and to the left, a second brown bird with darker brown and white wing stripes is seen on the ground among the grass. Near this bird sits a smaller, brown bird with white and dark streaked feathers. The color palette of the image includes various shades of brown, green, gray, black, white, and a hint of blue. The birds are primarily oriented along the left half and center of the image, with grass and leaves filling in the background on the lower half.

artworks.title: Brant Goose
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a pair of Brant Geese by the water's edge. The painting depicts two Brant Geese engaged in an interaction. One goose is perched on a rock with its wings folded against its body, while the other stands on a lower rock with wings partially spread. These rocks are set against a backdrop of distant rolling hills and a calm sea, under a sky that suggests a peaceful atmosphere. The detailing of the birds is intricate, with attention paid to the texture of their feathers and shading in their plumage. This is in the style of John James Audubon, known for detailed depictions of birds in their natural habitats.

artworks.title: Louisiana Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a hawk perched on a branch. The artwork features a detailed depiction of a hawk with intricately painted feathers displaying shades of brown, orange, and hints of white. The bird has a majestic and poised demeanor, with its piercing eye and sharp beak, while its talons clutch onto a branch. The background is a plain, off-white color which highlights the hawk. This is done in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Townsend's Warbler, Arctic Blue Bird and Western Blue Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows five colorful birds perched on intertwining branches with red flowers and green leaves. The birds display a variety of colors, including shades of blue, yellow, brown, and orange. A yellow and black bird is positioned at the top left, a bright blue bird with a reddish underbelly is on the right, a brown and white bird is in the center, a dark bird with blue and brown plumage is at the bottom left, and an orange and blue bird is on the right. The birds are evenly distributed across the branches in different orientations.

artworks.title: Chestnut-colored Finch, Black-headed Siskin, Black Crown Bunting and Arctic Ground Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows several birds in various poses within a natural setting. The birds have different colors and patterns on their bodies. They are seen perched on branches and standing among tall grass and a blooming pink flower. The color scheme consists mostly of earthy tones with pops of yellow, black, white, and reddish-brown. Two birds are on the ground in the foreground, while two others are perched on a branch with one bird leaning towards a flower. A spider is visible on the flower.

artworks.title: Audubon's Warbler, Hermit Warbler and Black-throated Gray Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a cluster of six small birds perched on greenery with clusters of red flowers and berries. The color palette includes natural tones like greens, vibrant yellows, blues, and rich reds. The birds are positioned centrally amidst the branches with one bird clinging to a lower branch.

artworks.title: Burgomaster Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting features two seagulls perched on a rocky landscape against a dark background. One gull has white plumage, a yellow eye, and a yellow bill with a red spot on the lower mandible, standing on the foreground rock. The other gull has brown plumage and is lying on the rocks in the background. The painting shows detailed brushstrokes for the feathers, bill, and feet, and earthy tones for the rocks, indicating a coastal habitat. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Scarlet Ibis
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds standing beside a body of water. The painting features a vibrant red ibis with a long, curved bill standing in profile to the left, and a more subtly colored bird with shades of brown, perched on a small rock to the right. The background shows a serene waterway extending into the distance with soft cloud formations above.

artworks.title: Lazuli Finch, Clay-colored Finch and Oregon Snow Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts three birds perched on branches of a flowering plant. One bird has bright blue and orange plumage, the second has light brown and beige coloration, and the third has black, white, and brown feathers. The background features vibrant blues, oranges, pinks, soft browns, beiges, greens, and hints of black. The birds are positioned on different branches, with the blue and orange bird singing, the light brown bird sitting below, and the black, white, and brown bird on the lower branch. Pink flowers and green leaves adorn the branches.

artworks.title: Black-throated Green Warbler, Blackburnian Warbler and Mourning Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image contains five colorful birds on a branch with green leaves. The birds have shades of yellow, green, brown, black, and blue. They are positioned vertically on the branch, with two at the top left corner, two in the middle, and one at the bottom right. Brown branches and green leaves are scattered throughout the composition.

artworks.title: Arkansaw Siskin, Mealy Red-poll, Louisiana Tanager, Townsend's Finch and Buff-breasted Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting depicting five birds perched on branches and grass. The birds are uniquely colored and posed, sitting on various levels of a thin, winding branch and on the ground among grass. The topmost bird has pinkish hues and a red cap. A bird below it has bright yellow plumage with black wings. Another bird is grayish and rests on the branch's end, while the bird on the right has warm orange and black feathers. The painting emphasizes precise lines and delicate coloring to detail the birds' feathers and markings. The background subtly gives an impression of distance, evoking an open natural space. This piece is stylistically reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Red-breasted Merganser
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two ducks, one flying and one swimming, and aquatic plants. The scene captures detailed illustrations of two ducks, with one duck gliding through the sky and the other duck swimming across a calm body of water. Both ducks exhibit vibrant, intricately detailed feathers. To the left of the image, there are tall aquatic plants with long leaves and yellow flowers. The water has soft ripples and the sky is a gentle gradient of blue.

artworks.title: Black-throated Guillemot, Nobbed-billed Auk, Curled-Crested Auk and Horned-billed Guillemot
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting depicts several birds perched on ice with a mountainous backdrop. Different species of auk and guillemot birds are positioned on the icy shoreline, with a vast expanse of water and towering, snow-capped mountains in the background. The icy environment includes large chunks of ice on which the birds are resting or swimming nearby. Each bird has unique identifying features such as different body plumage patterns and beak shapes. The sky is a pale blue.

artworks.title: Golden-eye Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting depicts a golden-eye duck on the water. The duck is portrayed with various colors, from deep purple on the head to iridescent blue shades. The body transitions from white to dark colors, blending with the water. The image includes gentle ripples in the water to show the duck's movement. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Eared Grebe
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two Eared Grebes. The painting depicts two birds in detail on a rocky surface near a body of water. Tall grassy reeds are visible in the background, under a pale blue sky.

artworks.title: Semi-palmated Sandpiper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two semipalmated sandpipers on a rocky shoreline adorned with seashells. The drawing depicts two small birds with greyish-brown plumage, white underbellies, and black beaks perched on the edge of a rock. Various colored seashells are scattered across the rock. In the background, there is a body of water, distant hills, and a pastel sky. The composition emphasizes the natural setting and the intricate details of the birds and shells.

artworks.title: Trumpeter Swan
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of a swan swimming in a body of water. The print depicts the swan with its body facing the left and its long neck curved back towards the right, its head looking down at a small moth or butterfly on the surface of the water. Its black beak is partially open to reveal small, pointed teeth. The feathers of the swan are detailed, with a gradient of white to light gray. Its black, webbed foot is partially submerged under the green-gray water, creating small ripples. The background is a blue sky with blue-gray clouds.

artworks.title: Dusky Albatros
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Dusky Albatross perched near a body of water. The bird is shown with a strong build, a black beak, and brownish-black feathers with detailed wing patterns. The scene depicts the bird on a rocky outcrop overlooking the sea with crashing waves below. The background is softly shaded to emphasize the bird. The style is similar to John James Audubon's bird illustrations.
